newsitem.title: USA: EU meat negotiators to return to U.S. Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: EU meat negotiators to return to U.S. Wednesday.

text.p: EU officials trying to negotiate an agreement with the United States to resolve a dispute over meat imports are set to return to Washington on Wednesday, an Agriculture Department official said.

The USDA official said the negotiators will be discussing issues relating to the meat talks, but would not say what implications this latest development meant for Washington's plan to remove some 100 EU meat and poultry plants from its list of approved exporters on Wednesday if the plants do not meet U.S. inspection standards.

The USDA is expected to make an announcement Tuesday on whether or not an agrement has been reached in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks, and whether it will follow through with its threatened plan to delist the EU plants.
Delisting the plants would halt some $300 million worth of EU meat imports to the United States, mostly pork products from Denmark and Italian hams.
U.S. industry sources said USDA was seriously considering reaching an agreement without including poultry, which has proved to be the key obstacle to a settlement.
They speculated the negotiators could be returning to Washington to continue talks on how to resolve the remaining poultry issues.

On April 1, the EU implemented new inspection regulations that have halted the flow of U.S. poultry to Europe. The new rules could block the shipment of some $50 million worth of U.S. poultry exports.
